files.content:
# todo-cli

A tiny to-do list for the command line. It keeps your to-dos in a JSON file
in the current folder, so each project folder can have its own list.

## Usage

```sh
node src/index.js add "Buy oat milk"
node src/index.js list
node src/index.js done 2
node src/index.js remove 1
```

`list` prints every to-do with its number. `done` and `remove` take that
number. Set `TODO_FILE` to keep the list somewhere else:

```sh
TODO_FILE=~/todos.json node src/index.js list
```

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

The tests use Node's built-in test runner (Node 18 or newer). There are no
dependencies to install.

worker.about: A careful, fair code reviewer. Follow the craftbook steps exactly, read the code you are given, and report only problems you can point to in a line.

success.summary: The review-code-folder task read the sample folder, wrote review.md with all three sections, found the off-by-one in removeTodo and the unsaved done flag in completeTodo with their lines, and reached its terminal step without external services.

checks.label: the done flag that is never saved

axes.name: accuracy
axes.description: The findings are the two real defects (removeTodo removes the item after the one asked for; completeTodo never saves the done flag), each with its file and line, and no invented bugs.

axes.name: usefulness
axes.description: Each finding has a fair severity, a concrete example of what goes wrong, and a fix a developer could apply as written.

rubric.contextNote: Advisory only. Deterministic pass/fail comes from the craftbook runtime gates, the deliverable checks, attribution, and terminal progress.
